messages.author: c4a3575d08613e47
messages.subject: Seemingly Unrelated Regression (SUR)?
parts:
Hi everyone.

Is seemingly unrelated regression possible with INLA? If so how do you call it? 

As always I apologize in advance for potentially asking an obvious question.

Kind regards, Claus Vestergaard

messages.author: f66907f526d3c7bf
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Seemingly Unrelated Regression (SUR)?
parts:
Up to 5 equations should be do-able, using an iid5d latent model (http://www.math.ntnu.no/inla/r-inla.org/doc/latent/iid123d.pdf): you just need to extend the first example to include covariates: basically you can stack the data, and apply the same model to each (but include an interaction with a factor that says what column the datum is). There might be more efficient ways of writing the model, but my inla-indexing foo isn't up to it.

With more than 5 covariates, I think you would need to introduce structure somehow, and that will be context dependent.

Bob

messages.author: f66907f526d3c7bf
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Seemingly Unrelated Regression (SUR)?
parts:
I've been working with models where a higher number would be needed (e.g. dx.doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.12180), but I agree that the number of hyperparameters is going to be the problem - I assume the computational costs get huge. I don't know if it's practicable to generalise the function to iidXd and let the user worry if X is so large their computation becomes a major contributor to global warming. So, in practice an extension to 7d, and beyond, would be attractive, but I don't know how much effort it would take.

Bob
